scope: Player connection and client state only. No server-only instrumentation.

channels.label: Health and hunger
channels.description: Saturation and oxygen are client-held values; no server exhaustion or hidden damage state.

channels.label: Attributes
channels.description: Only attributes received by this connection; unknown values are not inferred.

channels.label: Locally simulated movement
channels.description: Client physics estimates, not authoritative server internals.

channels.label: Inventory and equipment
channels.description: Slot indices use Minecraft window coordinates; item details include client-received NBT, durability and enchantments.

channels.label: Item cooldowns
channels.description: Packet durations tracked against actual client world ticks; never server-only attack cooldown.

channels.label: Nearby client-known blocks
channels.description: Includes occluded but client-received terrain, as a normal client cache does. Unloaded cells are unknown. No world files are read.

channels.label: Loaded chunk coverage
channels.description: Coverage metadata only. Full incoming chunk payloads are available through protocol.packets.

channels.label: Client-known block entity updates
channels.description: Only server-sent NBT; unopened container inventories are not queried.

channels.label: Received map pixels and icons
channels.description: Map patches retain their x/y offsets and sequence; never silently substitute a complete map.

channels.label: Line-of-sight entities
channels.description: Only client-received entities with unobstructed sampled sight rays; entity geometry is approximate and marked.

channels.label: Player list
channels.description: Tab-list data delivered by the server. Protected viewer players are excluded.

channels.label: Open container or trading window
channels.description: Only windows actually opened by this agent.

channels.label: Recipes and recipe book
channels.description: Use actual server declarations and unlocks, not all theoretical crafting recipes.

channels.label: Advancement definitions and progress
channels.description: Only data sent to the client; this does not request privileged advancement state.

channels.label: Statistics
channels.description: Available when the server sends statistics, normally on opening that UI. No privileged queries.

channels.label: Command suggestions
channels.description: Server-provided accessible command tree and tab-completion responses only.

channels.label: Resource pack offer
channels.description: Offers are recorded; untrusted URLs are never fetched automatically.

channels.label: Heard sound events
channels.description: Includes named, numeric, entity-attached, note/block/world sounds and stop commands. Raw protocol preserves exact fields.

channels.label: Chat and UI messages
channels.description: Includes messages addressed to this connection and action bars.

channels.label: First-person depth and semantic image
channels.description: CPU projection from received collision shapes and entity bounds. Not a vanilla RGB screenshot; transparent surfaces and non-collision decorations are approximate.

channels.label: Rendered RGB capture
channels.description: Actual first-person pixels from the managed Fabric client framebuffer, or an authenticated external producer for other backends. Mineflayer does not launch a renderer itself.

channels.label: Decoded server-sound PCM
channels.description: Actual vanilla Ogg samples mixed from received sound events. Omits client-only ambience/music/footsteps generated locally and resource-pack overrides; use audio.capture for exact client output.

channels.label: Actual rendered client audio
channels.description: PCM from a real client audio producer; unavailable until fresh frames are supplied.

channels.label: Every incoming PLAY packet
channels.description: Opt-in high-volume catch-all. Preserves all decoded PLAY fields, byte arrays as base64, 64-bit values as tagged integers. Excludes login/auth traffic; bounded loss is explicitly reported.

limitations: No server-only data or world-file access
Protocol capture is opt-in and bounded; losses are reported
Depth and semantic geometry are native; exact RGB requires a rendered client producer
Server-sound PCM omits client-generated ambience and resource-pack overrides; exact audio requires a client capture producer
Events are retained in a finite rolling window and carry sequence numbers
Unsent statistics, unopened container inventory and unloaded terrain are unavailable
